title: One Rounding Fits All: Memory-Efficient Approximation Algorithms for Partition-Constrained Influence Maximization

problem.claim: Partition-constrained influence maximization seeks to select multiple user sets that participate in influencing users in complex viral-marketing settings.

gap.claim: The existing RAMP algorithm has prohibitive memory overhead from maintaining 1/ε intermediate subsets during rounding and sample inefficiency from requiring an additional RR-set collection for solution evaluation.

contributions.claim: RBwA is a memory-efficient and sample-efficient progressive sampling algorithm for partition-constrained influence maximization.
RBwA uses Rademacher average to estimate solution quality directly, eliminating additional validation sets and reducing rounding invocations to one.
BwARound is a memory-efficient rounding scheme that stores one fractional vector and takes maximal feasible steps for coverage maximization subroutines.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that RBwA and BwARound provide significant improvements in space complexity and iteration count over RAMP's AMPRound.
The authors report extensive experiments on large-scale social networks demonstrating the effectiveness of RBwA and BwARound.

narrative_sequence.summary: Influence maximization selects influential individuals, but modern viral-marketing scenarios increasingly require multiple participating user sets.
IM-PC was formulated as a general partition-constrained influence-maximization problem, with RAMP providing a tight approximation guarantee.
RAMP is limited by high rounding memory overhead and the need for a separate RR-set collection for evaluation.
RBwA uses direct solution-quality estimation through Rademacher average, while BwARound reduces stored state and uses maximal feasible rounding steps.
Experiments on large-scale social networks are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
